items.title: Replit built a security model for its desktop app with Windows
items.takeaway: Amjad Masad calls desktop AI apps a security and privacy nightmare in general. He says Replit worked with Windows on a security model for Replit Desktop, and Christie's chose Replit for secure agentic work.
items.soWhat: Ask any desktop agent vendor how it limits what the agent can reach on your machines.

items.title: Rauch warns free stealth-model inference can be data exfiltration
items.takeaway: Guillermo Rauch, quoting a viral post about a provider offering a stealth model, argues that 'free' inference marketed as zero data retention is a way to move data to nation states at scale. It is his opinion.
items.soWhat: Treat free or unnamed model endpoints as a data risk until you know who runs them.

items.title: Pocock: early codebase skill built his best greenfield project yet
items.takeaway: Matt Pocock asked what should go in a '/the-perfect-typescript-codebase' skill. He then said an early version produced the best codebase he has made, on a greenfield project.
items.soWhat: Encoding your team's codebase standards as an agent skill may raise output quality from day one.

items.title: OpenAI proposes perplexity as the shared metric for pacing labs
items.takeaway: OpenAI published 'Perplexity and Intelligence', which reached 437 points on Hacker News. swyx summarizes it as proposing perplexity, not FLOPS, as the universal metric for industry self-regulation and pacing.
items.soWhat: If labs adopt one metric for limits, it will frame how regulators and buyers judge model progress.

items.title: Kun Chen shares a /vision skill for agents that keep asking you
items.takeaway: Kun Chen published a video on his '/vision' skill, meant for agents that keep asking the human for decisions. He says it helps when the human's judgment is the bottleneck.
items.soWhat: Writing down your intent once can cut how often agents stop to ask you.
